purpose: Aripiprazole lauroxil is used to treat schizophrenia in adults. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. Because it is a long-acting injection, you do not have to take a pill every day.
how_it_works: This medication works by balancing certain chemical messengers in your brain, particularly dopamine and serotonin. When these chemicals are out of balance, they can cause symptoms of schizophrenia. By steadying these signals, the medication helps your brain function more normally and keeps symptoms under control.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include injection site pain or soreness, weight gain, feeling restless or having an urge to move around (akathisia), drowsiness, headache, and constipation. Some people may also feel dizzy when standing up quickly.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have diabetes or a family history of it, since this medicine can affect blood sugar. It may cause a rare but serious movement disorder called tardive dyskinesia with long-term use. Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis should not use this medication due to an increased risk of stroke or death. Avoid driving until you know how this medicine affects you.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection by a healthcare provider, not taken at home as a pill. Depending on the dose your doctor prescribes, you may receive the shot once a month, every 6 weeks, or every 2 months. Your doctor will decide the right schedule and dose for you, and you may need a starter injection or brief oral medication when you first begin.
